profile: HTML&HTML Open Website AI Readiness Audit Profile
disclaimer: This is an openly published HTML&HTML product audit profile, not an IETF, W3C, Google, OpenAI, Anthropic or other third-party standard.
principles: Measured facts, normative standards, vendor guidance, proposals and heuristics must remain distinguishable.
Unknown or unavailable evidence must not be forced into pass or fail.
A score describes measured technical conditions only; it does not guarantee ranking, traffic, revenue or AI citation.
Public scanning must not invent private source-code ownership or file paths.
Security boundaries must fail closed for private, local, reserved or credential-bearing targets.
Experimental agent surfaces must not be published solely to improve a score.

sourceClasses.meaning: Current first-party product or crawler guidance.
Emerging convention that is not treated as a mandatory standard.
Directly observed HTTP, HTML, header, robots or link evidence.
HTML&HTML decision-support rule where no normative threshold exists.
Early or optional capability with limited maturity or adoption.

engines.name: Crawl & Index
engines.purpose: Public reachability, redirects, robots, sitemap, indexability and page discovery.

engines.name: Technical SEO
engines.purpose: Titles, descriptions, headings, canonicals, duplicate and route-level technical signals.

engines.name: AI / GEO Access
engines.purpose: Search, retrieval and AI crawler policy signals without conflating search access with training controls.

engines.name: llms.txt v2
engines.purpose: Proposal-format, link reachability and discovery relations such as describedby and Markdown alternates.

engines.name: Structured Data
engines.purpose: JSON-LD parseability, entity types and visible-identity consistency signals.

engines.name: Performance Hygiene
engines.purpose: Observable HTML/script/render-blocking hygiene; field CWV remain NOT_MEASURED without reliable field or lab data.

engines.name: Accessibility
engines.purpose: Document language, image alternatives, programmatic labels and accessible control names.

engines.name: Security Baseline
engines.purpose: HTTPS, browser security headers, mixed-content and insecure-form baseline controls.

engines.name: Content Trust
engines.purpose: Organization identity, contact, privacy, terms and editorial accountability signals.

engines.name: Agent Readiness
engines.purpose: Machine-readable and programmatic discovery surfaces while keeping experimental protocols explicitly optional.

engines.name: Conversion
engines.purpose: Visibility and continuity of public next-step/contact/form flows without changing business logic.

engines.name: Link Integrity
engines.purpose: Real HTTP probing of owned internal destinations and unnecessary redirects.
